description: Web ACL without Any Rate Based Rule
rationale: Every other kind of rule decides on one request at a time, so a client sending requests that are individually valid is never refused however many it sends. That is what a credential stuffing run, a scraping job and an application layer flood all look like: well formed requests, in volume, from a small number of sources. A rate based rule is the only statement in a web ACL that reacts to the volume a source sends rather than to the contents of a single request.
remediation: Add a rate based rule to the web ACL, scoped down to the paths that are expensive or that authenticate, with a limit set above the volume the legitimate traffic reaches
